name: Picture naming
readme:
[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.82901%2Fnemar.on006233-blue)](https://doi.org/10.82901/nemar.on006233)
This dataset, used in the analysis reported by Kochi et al., (2025), contains intracranial EEG recordings from 108 individuals who performed an picture‑naming task. Electrode coordinates are provided in MNI‑305 space.
Each EDF file is tagged for the auditory naming task with the following event codes:
401 – stimulus onset
501 – response onset
Reference:
Ryuzaburo Kochi, Aya Kanno, Hiroshi Uda, Keisuke Hatano, Hidenori Endo, Michael Cools, Robert Rothermel, Aimee F. Luat, Eishi Asano. Naming is Shaped by Early Facilitative and Late Compensatory Neural Interactions: An Intracranial Study of 125 Patients
## Channel names follow the data headers (18 Oct 2026)
In 347 recordings the channel list of channels.tsv did not equal the data-file header (names, order or count). In the 347 with a different channel count, `mne_bids.read_raw_bids` warned and kept the header names, so the channels.tsv types and bad-channel status reached only the channels whose names happen to be identical; a reader that applies the channels.tsv rows by position gives wrong labels wherever the two lists are not aligned. Since 18 Oct 2026 every channels.tsv lists exactly the header channels, in header order, with the header names (MNE names: duplicated header labels numbered -0, -1).
Rows were matched to header channels BY NAME, never by position (exact; then case/whitespace; then the recorder prefix 'EEG '/'POL ', '_' and zero padding; then a trailing '-<reference>' token). Matched rows keep all their columns (type, units, status, ...); 0 rows took the header name.
17354 header channels had no channels.tsv row (347 files) and got a new row: type from the name (ECG/EMG/EOG/trigger) or from the other contacts of the same shaft, else MISC; units from the header; status n/a. Examples: `sub-007_ses-1_task-picture_ieeg.edf`: POL A1-A2, POL A11-A12, POL A17-A18, POL A23-A24; `sub-007_ses-2_task-picture_ieeg.edf`: POL A26-A31, POL A27-A32, POL DC01, POL DC02; `sub-007_ses-3_task-picture_ieeg.edf`: POL B1-B2, POL B17-B18, POL B25-B26, POL B33-B34.
44820 channels.tsv rows had no channel in the data file (347 files) and were removed; they are kept verbatim under `sourcedata/channels-removed-2026-10-18/` (same relative path). Examples: `sub-007_ses-1_task-picture_ieeg.edf`: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5; `sub-007_ses-2_task-picture_ieeg.edf`: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5; `sub-007_ses-3_task-picture_ieeg.edf`: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5.
Applied by position, the former rows would have given wrong labels to 17352 channels in 347 files (rows missing, extra or out of order before that position).
Bipolar data: in 344 files the data header holds bipolar derivations named after two contacts (e.g. `POL A1-A2`), while channels.tsv listed the monopolar contacts (`A1`, `A2`, ...). A derivation is not matched to the row of its first contact: each of the 16648 bipolar channels got its own row (type = the type of both contacts, `reference` = the second contact, columns shared by both contact rows copied, `status` bad when either contact was bad (5607 rows), good when both were good (11041 rows)), and the contact rows not recorded as such moved to `sourcedata/channels-removed-2026-10-18/`. electrodes.tsv (contact positions) is unchanged; a derivation `X-Y` lies between contacts X and Y.
## Electrode locations (19 Oct 2026; revised 22 Oct 2026)
Add coordsystem.json MNI305/mm next to 347 electrodes.tsv. Evidence: Wayne State (Asano/Kanno/Kochi) deposits use FreeSurfer-standard (MNI305/fsaverage) electrode coordinates; MNI305 is a millimetre space by definition. No OpenNeuro S3 version of this dataset ever held a coordsystem.json (all versions listed 2026-10-19). README: "Electrode coordinates are provided in MNI-305 space." Paper PMC12746732 ("Intracranial Electrodes"): "electrode coordinates were aligned to the FreeSurfer standard brain".
Primary source: this dataset's own README (line 3 of README.md on main, nemarDatasets/on006233@396692f0), quoted above.
Reproducible check (22 Oct 2026): for each of the 347 electrodes.tsv, every contact's x/y/z was compared (to 0.001 mm) with every electrodes.tsv of other deposits from the same group at pinned nemarDatasets commits (on004551@c4c035f6, on004859@db21ebb2, on005007@b59363aa, on005545@948f2825, on005931@cbd529e5, on006107@b37dcbfc, on006910@9eb96ebd, on006914@1956b035, on007118@8f2c41fa, on007119@c099745b, on007120@66296ebd). 347 files have all contacts identical to one file of another deposit: 198 to a deposit whose coordsystem.json declares fsaverage/mm (on007118, on007119, on007120) and 347 to a deposit whose README states MNI305/MNI-305 (on004551, on005545, on006910, on006914); a file can match both.
Limitation: these sidecars declare the frame and units only. electrodes.tsv is unchanged and no coordinate value changed. Positions do not attach to channels in mne_bids or EEGDash, because the channel names (data-header labels, e.g. prefixed labels or bipolar derivations) differ from the contact names in electrodes.tsv; a channel-to-contact mapping is not part of this change. This dataset mirrors OpenNeuro; the same change belongs upstream.
## Units of the picture-naming recordings (20 Nov 2026)
The EDF headers of the picture-naming recordings label the unit "V", but the values are microvolts (for example, the physical range of sub-007 ses-1 is about ±934 and ±243, which is not plausible in volts).
The `units` column of every `*_task-picture_channels.tsv` therefore says `µV` (micro sign, U+00B5).
## Electrode coordinate frame (20 Nov 2026)
The coordsystem.json files declare `fsaverage` (millimeters) instead of `MNI305`.
Every contact's x/y/z in the 347 electrodes.tsv (39567 contacts) equals a vertex of the FreeSurfer fsaverage pial surface (left or right hemisphere) within 0.001 mm, which is the signature of FreeSurfer surface-based normalization to the fsaverage template.
The volumetric frame of fsaverage is FreeSurfer's MNI305 space, which is why the README above calls the space MNI-305.
No coordinate value changed.
